11-3121.00:990.short: Field manager and employee questions, apply contracts and CAO to cases, help resolve work problems.

steps.what: Receive question or issue by mail, Teams, phone or on the floor

loop.input: free-text question from Teams or mail
loop.output: category (general policy, contract, personal case, conflict) plus urgency
loop.check: category must be in a fixed list; personal and conflict categories always route to the HRBP of that site
loop.stop: one pass; low confidence or no category goes to the HRBP queue unclassified
loop.why_not_simpler: questions arrive as free text in Dutch and English; a form alone is ignored by shift managers

steps.what: Look up contract, CAO article, absence and history in AFAS and SharePoint
Interpret contract and CAO for this case and decide HR position

loop.input: case brief plus retrieved CAO and contract clauses
loop.output: draft reading of the relevant clauses with citations
loop.check: every claim must cite a clause id that exists in the indexed CAO or contract template; uncited text is dropped
loop.stop: one draft; if no clause found it says so and the HRBP works from scratch
loop.why_not_simpler: matching a messy situation to clause text needs reading free text

steps.what: Talk with manager and employee to resolve the problem
Record outcome, send confirmation letter, request contract change in AFAS

11-3121.00:990.design: A Teams front door (Copilot Studio or a small app on the M365 tenant) takes questions, classifies them with one bounded model call and answers general policy from the indexed SharePoint and CAO content; personal and conflict cases open a case in a SharePoint list with an auto-built case brief from the AFAS API. The HRBP gets a draft clause reading with citations, does the conversation, and a Power Automate flow turns the agreed outcome into a template letter and an AFAS change request for HR admin.
11-3121.00:990.previous_blocker: Questions arrive as unstructured talk and mail, and pulling contract, absence and CAO context took manual clicks in three places.
11-3121.00:990.enabler_now: AFAS Profit connectors and cheap retrieval over owned documents make a case brief and a cited clause draft a few days of build.
11-3121.00:990.still_hard: Trust from shift workers and managers who expect a person, and cases where the facts are disputed; the model must never decide a personal case.
11-3121.00:990.human_edge: Reading the room between a site manager and a worker, choosing what to concede, and being trusted by both sides.

ambition.what: Night and weekend shift workers in the warehouses get answers to contract and roster questions in their own shift instead of waiting for an office-hours HRBP.

11-3121.00:990.altitude: The HRBP spends less time looking things up and more time on the 20-30 real conflicts per month per site; they decide which case categories the desk may answer alone.

reach.learn: Which change requests arrive incomplete and what fields the template must force.
Which CAO allowance questions keep coming back so the desk can answer them from payroll rules.

evidence.claim: IBM's Ask HR handles over 11 million interactions a year, with HRBPs as first human support for escalated complex cases.
Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves 1,200 of 3,600 staff monthly and opens tickets for what it cannot answer.
Employee-facing bots must disclose they are AI.
Works council consent is needed before AI processes personnel data.
AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors and UpdateConnectors usable for a case brief.

assumptions: The CAO texts and contract templates are current in SharePoint.
Most questions from managers repeat across the three sites.
unknowns: Share of questions that are personal cases versus general policy.
Whether the OR will consent to case logging of questions about named employees.
Whether IT allows an AFAS API user with read access to contracts and absence.
research_questions: Of last month's 100 HRBP mails and Teams threads, how many could be answered from policy text alone?
Does the case brief cut lookup time by more than half in a two-week shadow test?
Do shift workers actually use a Teams bot, or do they need a phone or kiosk channel?

11-3121.00:991.short: Set weekly priorities for the 13-person HR team, chase status, approve exceptions, coach direct reports.

steps.what: Collect status from HRBPs, recruiters, payroll and admin by mail and Teams
Weekly priorities and workload review in an Excel tracker and team meeting
Approve escalations: contract changes, pay exceptions, dismissal routes
One-to-ones, coaching and performance talks with direct reports
Write monthly HR update for the management team

loop.input: HR metric extract with month-on-month changes and the director's short notes
loop.check: all figures inserted by code from the metric layer; model text may not contain numbers not in the extract; director reads before sending
loop.stop: one draft plus up to two regenerations; on failure fall back to the fixed template with figures only
loop.why_not_simpler: the explanation of why metrics moved is free text that a template cannot write

11-3121.00:991.design: Replace the Excel tracker and the status mail round with a Power BI team-workload page fed nightly from AFAS (absence cases, mutations), Recruitee (open vacancies, stage age) and Studytube (overdue certificates), plus Teams notifications when an item breaches its agreed age. Exceptions run through configured AFAS workflow approvals with CAO-table pre-checks, and a small drafting step writes the MT update around code-inserted figures.
11-3121.00:991.previous_blocker: Status lived in three systems and people's heads; building cross-system views cost more analyst time than the chasing it saved.
11-3121.00:991.enabler_now: AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube all expose APIs and Power BI already holds a nightly AFAS extract; AI-assisted coding makes the joins and alert rules a matter of days.
11-3121.00:991.still_hard: Case age is a weak proxy for case difficulty; the dashboard will flag slow cases that are slow for good reasons.
11-3121.00:991.human_edge: Coaching HRBPs, weighing a manager's request against fairness across sites, and carrying accountability for approvals stay with the director.

ambition.what: Re-balance team workload weekly across the three sites instead of at quarterly planning.

11-3121.00:991.altitude: Less chasing, more time on direct reports; the director gains the right to set which exception types auto-approve within CAO bounds and which always need sign-off.

reach.task: maintain the HR metric layer behind Power BI
reach.learn: how case age and stage age are defined so alert thresholds mean something
which mutation types fail checks most often

evidence.claim: HR platforms let the HR lead set which tasks run alone, which need review and log every approver.
AFAS Profit supports workflow approvals on mutations.
Workload dashboards that show per-person case counts can be treated as employee monitoring and need works council consent.

assumptions: The AFAS extract in Power BI already includes absence cases and mutations.
Recruitee API access is available on the current licence.
unknowns: Whether the OR sees a per-employee workload view as a monitoring system under WOR art. 27.
Which AFAS workflows are already configured for approvals.
How many exceptions per month reach the director today.
research_questions: How many hours a week do the director and team spend on status mail and the tracker?
Can the team-level view be aggregated so no individual HR employee is tracked, avoiding consent?
Which exception types could be pre-approved within CAO tables without legal risk?

11-3121.00:987.short: Answer managers' policy questions, advise on harassment and equal treatment cases, propose policy changes.

steps.what: Receive manager questions by mail, Teams and phone
Look up policy, CAO article or law and answer routine questions

loop.input: manager question plus retrieved passages from SharePoint policies and both CAOs
loop.output: short answer with cited article and link, or a hand-off to HR
loop.check: answer must cite a retrieved passage; a classifier routes harassment, discrimination, dismissal, medical and pay-dispute topics to a person before any answer
loop.stop: one answer attempt; no citation or low retrieval score means hand-off to the HRBP queue
loop.why_not_simpler: managers ask in free text and the answer lives in long documents; an FAQ page alone has not been used

steps.what: Draft written advice to a manager on a sensitive case

loop.input: director's case notes and the relevant policy passages
loop.output: draft advice with steps, deadlines and cited rules
loop.check: director edits and signs; draft runs on the governed tenant, no special-category data leaves it
loop.stop: one draft, regenerate on request; fallback is the director writing it
loop.why_not_simpler: each case differs; a template covers the structure, not the reasoning

steps.what: Judge harassment, discrimination and conflict cases and talk with the manager
Notice recurring issues and propose policy changes

11-3121.00:987.design: A Teams policy desk answers routine manager questions from SharePoint policies and the two CAOs with cited articles, discloses that it is an assistant (AI Act Art. 50) and hands sensitive topics straight to the HRBP queue. Every question is logged; a monthly Power BI page shows question themes by site, which feeds policy proposals, and the director drafts sensitive advice with a bounded drafting step.
11-3121.00:987.previous_blocker: Policies and CAO texts were too long and inconsistent for keyword search, and a wrong answer on law carries legal cost.
11-3121.00:987.enabler_now: Retrieval with forced citation now answers from long documents reliably enough for routine questions, with routing as the safety net.
11-3121.00:987.still_hard: Keeping SharePoint policies current and consistent; a stale document gives a confidently cited wrong answer.
11-3121.00:987.human_edge: Hearing both sides in a harassment case, weighing credibility and protecting the reporter cannot be delegated.

ambition.what: Shift leads and team leaders in the Tilburg and Venlo warehouses, who rarely reach HR today, get answers at night and on weekend shifts.

11-3121.00:987.altitude: Fewer interruptions on routine questions; the director decides which topics the desk may answer and owns the hand-off list.

reach.learn: which escalations the desk should have answered and which it should never touch
how pay questions are phrased so the desk retrieves the right table

evidence.claim: IBM's AskHR handled 16 million messages in 2025 with CSAT +74, after an early failure from removing human routes too fast.
At IBM India 90-95% of HR questions go through an assistant while managers keep decisions.
Chatbots must disclose they are AI under Art. 50 of the AI Act.
AI policy should be discussed with the works council in the Art. 24 meeting.

assumptions: Policies and CAO texts sit in SharePoint in a findable form.
Managers have Teams on their phones or shared terminals.
unknowns: How many manager questions arrive per month and what share is routine.
Whether warehouse shift leads have Teams accounts.
How current the SharePoint policy set is.
research_questions: Of last quarter's manager questions, what share could be answered from a cited policy passage?
Do shift leads in Venlo and Tilburg actually use Teams?
What error rate on a 100-question test set would HR accept before go-live?

11-3121.00:994.short: Pull HR data, find causes of turnover, absence and hiring problems, recommend policy changes.

steps.what: Request extracts from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and agency portals
Combine and clean data in Excel
Drill down by site, shift, manager and agency to find causes
Read exit interview notes and 90-day leaver comments for themes

loop.output: theme label per comment from a fixed list of 10-15 themes, with quote
loop.check: monthly sample of 20 labels checked by the HRBP; themes with fewer than 5 cases hidden to protect identity
loop.stop: one pass per comment; unclear goes to 'other' for manual read
loop.why_not_simpler: comments are free text in Dutch and other languages; keyword rules miss most of them

steps.what: Write recommendations and present to the management team

11-3121.00:994.design: Extend the nightly AFAS extract into a governed metric layer that also loads Recruitee stages, Studytube completions and agency hours, and publish fixed Power BI pages for the North Star: hire-to-day-90 retention, time to hire, week-one onboarding and verzuim by site, shift and agency. A bounded classification step tags pseudonymised exit comments into fixed themes; the director keeps the reading of causes and the recommendation.
11-3121.00:994.previous_blocker: Four sources with different employee keys and no analyst time to join them; every question became a one-off Excel job.
11-3121.00:994.enabler_now: Power BI and the AFAS extract already exist; AI-assisted coding makes the Recruitee, Studytube and agency joins cheap to build and maintain.
11-3121.00:994.still_hard: Matching flex workers from agency portals to later AFAS hires, and small group sizes per shift that make causes noisy and identities guessable.
11-3121.00:994.human_edge: Deciding which correlation is a cause, and which recommendation managers and the OR will accept, needs the director's knowledge of the sites.

ambition.what: Review 90-day retention by site and agency every month instead of once a year.

11-3121.00:994.altitude: From ordering numbers to reading them; the director decides each month which site or agency gets an intervention.

reach.task: build the metric layer and definitions
reach.learn: which drill-downs the director actually uses
how agency choice links to 90-day retention and cost per productive hire

evidence.claim: Personnel analysis is best served by a copilot on the people analyst's metric layer, giving scenarios not one number.
AFAS Profit 8 adds a match score for vacancies; scoring people is high-risk under the AI Act from Dec 2027.
Systems that evaluate or monitor workers become high-risk from 2 Dec 2027.

assumptions: Verzuim data in the extract holds no medical diagnosis, as Dutch law forbids recording it.
Agency portals offer hour exports.
unknowns: Whether agency portals carry a stable worker id that matches later AFAS records.
Where exit interview notes are stored and in what form.
Whether the OR must consent to new analyses of absence data.
research_questions: Can flex workers be matched to later direct hires in more than 80% of cases?
Are per-site, per-shift groups large enough to report without identifying people?
Does the existing Power BI licence and AFAS extract support adding three more sources?

11-3121.00:1001.short: Build the yearly HR personnel budget in Excel from AFAS data and CAO tables, then track it monthly.

steps.what: Export positions, salaries and contract hours from AFAS into the budget workbook
Apply CAO wage steps, indexation, pension, social charges and agency rates
Choose hiring, flex mix, training and wage-round assumptions per site
Agree the personnel budget with Finance Director and controller
Compare monthly actuals to budget and explain variances

11-3121.00:1001.design: Replace the budget workbook with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that reads AFAS positions and payroll, the agency invoices and a versioned CAO rate table, and writes a cost baseline plus editable scenario parameters. A Power BI page shows scenarios side by side and the monthly actual-versus-budget variance per site and cost type, refreshed with the nightly AFAS extract.
11-3121.00:1001.previous_blocker: CAO rules, agency rates and AFAS exports lived in separate files, and building a reliable rate engine cost more than one yearly Excel exercise.
11-3121.00:1001.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small, tested rate engine and data job cheap to build, and the nightly AFAS extract for Power BI already exists.
11-3121.00:1001.still_hard: Keeping the CAO rate table correct after each wage round, and flex costs that swing with seasonal volume.
11-3121.00:1001.human_edge: Choosing where to spend scarce money (wages, flex, training) and defending that choice with Finance and the works council.

ambition.what: Re-forecast the personnel budget monthly per site instead of once a year, including the cost of each CAO offer during the 2027 round.

11-3121.00:1001.altitude: Less time in Excel, more time on trade-offs; the director owns the scenario assumptions that Finance accepts as input.

reach.task: Workforce cost lines in the company forecast
reach.learn: Use the same rate table and baseline so HR and Finance stop reconciling two numbers.
Keep the rate table as versioned, tested data rather than formulas in a workbook.

evidence.claim: Budgets suit deterministic software built from AFAS positions and CAO tables.
The transport CAO ends 31 Dec 2026, so a 2027 wage round must be costed now.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract includes positions, contract hours and wage components.
Agency invoices can be exported from the three portals in a fixed format.
unknowns: Whether Finance already keeps a separate personnel cost model in AFAS or Excel.
How the own warehouse CAO wage table is stored and who maintains it.
research_questions: Does the AFAS extract give enough wage component detail to reproduce last year's payroll cost within 1%?
Can all three agency portals export hours and invoices on a schedule?
Will the controller accept the platform baseline as the single source for personnel cost?

11-3121.00:993.short: Compile monthly HR statistics from AFAS: hires, transfers, appraisals and absence rates, and keep the records clean.

steps.what: Export employee, contract and absence data from AFAS
Check and correct data quality in Excel, chase HR admin
Calculate hires, transfers, appraisal completion, verzuim rate and frequency
Build the monthly report pack in Excel and PowerPoint
Write commentary and send to HR Director and site management

loop.input: month's HR statistics per site with prior month and same month last year
loop.output: half-page commentary on movements over a set threshold
loop.check: code checks every figure and site name against the statistics table; no individual names or absence causes allowed
loop.stop: two drafts, then the analyst writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: choosing which of many movements to explain and phrasing it plainly varies each month

11-3121.00:993.design: The nightly AFAS extract feeds a Power BI semantic model with fixed measures for hires, transfers, appraisal completion and verzuim percentage and frequency per site (rates and durations only, minimum group of five). Deterministic checks run after each refresh and post missing end dates or open sick reports to the HR admin queue; a paginated report subscription replaces the Excel/PowerPoint pack, with a checked draft commentary the analyst edits.
11-3121.00:993.previous_blocker: The checks and calculations lived in the analyst's Excel workbooks, and the AFAS extract was built for finance, not for HR rules like Poortwachter timelines.
11-3121.00:993.enabler_now: AI coding makes it quick to turn the Excel logic into tested measures and check scripts; Power BI subscriptions and paginated reports are already in the licence.
11-3121.00:993.still_hard: Some records are wrong at source (late sick reports, missing transfer dates), so the HR admin must still correct them; appraisal data may not be in AFAS at all.
11-3121.00:993.human_edge: Explaining why verzuim rose at one site and deciding what the HR Director should hear, without exposing a small team or an individual case.

ambition.what: Verzuim and 90-day retention per site available and correct by working day 2 instead of mid-month

11-3121.00:993.altitude: The monthly pack goes from about two days of work to an hour of review. The analyst decides which data breaks block publication and owns the verzuim and retention definitions.

reach.task: Registering absence and contract mutations in AFAS
reach.learn: Why records arrive late, so checks flag the cause, not just the gap
Payroll's cut-off dates, so the report reconciles to the same headcount

evidence.claim: Absence data is health data under GDPR Art. 9
The Dutch AP fined a firm partly for recording the cause of sick leave
Personal data systems and tools able to observe performance need works-council consent
Power BI supports report subscriptions and paginated reports

assumptions: Appraisal status is recorded in AFAS or can be exported
The current Excel logic for verzuim matches the CAO and Poortwachter definitions HR uses
HR admins accept a check queue in Teams or AFAS workflow
unknowns: Where performance appraisals are recorded today
Whether AFAS sick-report fields contain free-text causes that must be excluded
Which sites have teams under five people
research_questions: How many hours did the last three monthly packs take, and where did corrections happen?
Do the deterministic checks find the same issues the analyst finds by hand over two months in parallel?
Does the HR Director use the commentary, or only the figures?

11-3121.00:995.short: Plan the HR year: training, certificates, works council and union agenda, HR budget with Finance.

steps.what: Build the annual HR plan and calendar
Track mandatory certificates (forklift, VCA, food safety) from Studytube exports
Prepare works council and union dossiers, cost CAO demands

loop.input: union demand letters and FNV/CNV publications
loop.output: structured list of demands with parameters (percent, effective date, scope)
loop.check: director confirms each extracted parameter; costing runs in deterministic code on AFAS payroll data
loop.stop: one extraction pass; unclear demands flagged for manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: demands arrive as prose letters; the costing itself is plain code

steps.what: Agree HR and flex worker budget with Finance
Consult the works council and negotiate with unions

11-3121.00:995.design: Configure Studytube expiry alerts and a Power BI certificate page joined to AFAS rosters so forklift and VCA gaps reach shift leads before they lapse. A Python costing model on the governed data platform prices CAO demands and budget scenarios from AFAS payroll and agency hours, with a bounded extraction step reading union demand letters; the director keeps the plan, the OR consultation and the bargaining.
11-3121.00:995.previous_blocker: Costing CAO demands meant rebuilding payroll logic in Excel each round, and certificate tracking depended on manual exports.
11-3121.00:995.enabler_now: Studytube has native expiry reminders; AI-assisted coding makes a reusable costing model affordable, and the 2027 transport CAO round is starting now.
11-3121.00:995.still_hard: Modelling the pension switch and the in-house warehouse CAO interactions; scenario assumptions remain a judgement call.
11-3121.00:995.human_edge: Building trust with the OR and unions and choosing what to trade at the table are the director's work.

ambition.what: Same-day costing of any union counter-proposal during the 2027 CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer round.

11-3121.00:995.altitude: More time at the bargaining table and with the OR; the director decides scenario assumptions and which AI uses go to the OR for consent.

reach.learn: which pay components the costing model must mirror exactly

reach.task: build the annual personnel cost budget
reach.learn: how CAO scenarios flow into the company forecast

evidence.claim: FNV asks for worker say over AI at the CAO table and AI-literacy training.
The transport CAO ends 31 Dec 2026, before the pension switch.
Budgets from AFAS positions and CAO tables suit deterministic software.
Studytube tracks certificates and sends expiry reminders.

assumptions: Studytube certificate records carry expiry dates.
Payroll exports from AFAS contain all CAO pay components.
unknowns: Whether Studytube expiry reminders are already switched on.
Who in Finance owns the flex worker budget today.
Whether the warehouse CAO is negotiated on the same calendar as the transport CAO.
research_questions: Can a costing model reproduce last year's CAO cost within 1% of actual payroll?
How many certificate lapses happened in the last 12 months and what did they cost?
Does the OR want to review the costing model's assumptions before the round?

11-3121.00:1003.short: Run job evaluation: describe jobs, score them in the function system, set the scale, handle objections.

steps.what: Collect evaluation request and current job description from manager
Rewrite description in standard format and find comparable reference jobs

loop.input: Manager's job description and the function house reference jobs
loop.output: Description in the standard template and three nearest reference jobs with differences listed
loop.check: C&B specialist checks against interview with the manager; no score is produced
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; else manual
loop.why_not_simpler: Job descriptions are free text in varying shapes; matching on titles fails.

steps.what: Score the job and place it in a salary scale in committee
Check cost and equal-pay effects for current job holders
Record grade in AFAS, inform employees, handle objections

11-3121.00:1003.design: Configure an AFAS workflow for evaluation requests with the description attached, and add a bounded model step that rewrites descriptions into the template and lists nearest reference jobs, without scoring. A Power BI page shows the cost and pay-gap effect of a proposed grade; the committee scores, and AFAS generates the letter after approval.
11-3121.00:1003.previous_blocker: Descriptions arrived as free text in mail, and matching them to the function house needed an expert reading each one.
11-3121.00:1003.enabler_now: Models now rewrite and compare job texts reliably, and the AFAS workflow and Power BI extract already exist.
11-3121.00:1003.still_hard: Scoring remains judgement, objections are personal, and the works council must trust that the method is neutral.
11-3121.00:1003.human_edge: Weighing a job's real content fairly and explaining a grade face to face when someone objects.

ambition.what: An equal-pay check per job family, refreshed yearly, ready for the EU pay transparency rules.

11-3121.00:1003.altitude: The director chairs fewer, better prepared committees and owns the reference job set.

reach.learn: Maintain reference jobs as structured data the drafting step can use.
Start from the standard job description so vacancy and grade match.

evidence.claim: Job evaluation fits a copilot at autonomy 2; rate jobs, not people.
A ranking tool on people is high-risk from 2 Dec 2027 even with a final human click; tools without a score on people can fall outside.
A works council can have advice or consent rights over an AI decision.

assumptions: Noordhaven uses a function system (CAO grid or a method such as ORBA) with reference jobs on file.
The drafting step never scores jobs or people.
unknowns: Which job evaluation method each CAO prescribes and who holds its licence.
Whether the works council sees this change as needing consent under Art. 27 WOR.
research_questions: Do C&B reviewers accept at least 80% of drafted descriptions with small edits?
Does the function method licence allow using its reference texts in a model prompt?
Does the works council agree that a no-score drafting step is outside high-risk use?

11-3121.00:984.short: Match staff to roles, shifts and sites: redeployment, internal moves, peak-season staffing.

steps.what: Collect staffing needs and vacancies from site managers
Gather available staff, contract hours, valid certificates and absence
Shortlist matches, weigh fit, preferences and reintegration limits
Agree moves with managers and employees
Process change in AFAS, tell payroll and agency

11-3121.00:984.design: Replace the site Excel sheets with a Power Apps request form and a nightly job on the existing Power BI extract that joins AFAS contracts and absence, Studytube certificates and agency headcount into a filterable availability view with hard-rule filters (valid forklift or VCA, contract hours, CAO working-time limits). The HRBP picks matches by hand; a Power Automate flow sends approved moves to HR admin and the agency order.
11-3121.00:984.previous_blocker: Certificate, contract and absence data sit in three systems and the agency portals, so matching ran on memory and Excel.
11-3121.00:984.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the join, filters and form a short build on data that already reaches Power BI nightly.
11-3121.00:984.still_hard: No ranking or scoring of people: allocating tasks on traits or behaviour is high-risk under Annex III 4(b) from December 2027 and needs OR consent; agency portal data may only come as files.
11-3121.00:984.human_edge: Knowing who works well together, who is fragile after absence, and negotiating a move a person accepts.

ambition.what: Weekly redeployment review across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before ordering flex workers, instead of each site ordering agency staff alone.

11-3121.00:984.altitude: The HRBP reviews a cross-site availability view weekly and decides internal moves before agency orders go out.

reach.learn: How to add Studytube certificates and agency headcount to the model.
How internal moves change agency spend per site.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers structure and staffing without asking HR.
AI allocating tasks on behaviour or traits is high-risk from 2 December 2027.
OR consent is needed for systems that can observe behaviour or performance.

assumptions: Studytube has an export or API for certificate expiry dates.
Reintegration limits are recorded in AFAS absence cases.
unknowns: How the three agency portals export orders and headcount.
How often internal moves happen per month per site.
Whether sites will give up their own staffing sheets.
research_questions: In the last peak season, how many agency orders could have been filled by idle certified staff on another site?
Can Studytube certificate data be joined to AFAS employee ids reliably?
Will the OR accept a view showing absence status next to availability?

11-3121.00:1000.short: Forecast staffing needs per site and shift from volume plans, turnover and absence.

steps.what: Gather headcount, turnover, absence and flex hours per site
Collect volume and client forecasts from operations and site managers
Model demand per site and shift, attrition, retirements and absence
Choose scenarios: hire, flex, overtime or training per site
Present the plan to management and Finance

11-3121.00:1000.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform builds the workforce baseline from AFAS and the agency portals, and a small form (Microsoft Forms or a SharePoint list) collects site volume plans in a fixed format. A deterministic model with stated assumptions turns them into FTE need per site and shift under three scenarios in Power BI, feeding the budget and the recruiters' pipeline.
11-3121.00:1000.previous_blocker: Volume plans came in different shapes by mail, and agency hours were not joined to AFAS data.
11-3121.00:1000.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract and cheap AI-assisted coding make the joins and a transparent scenario model a few days of work.
11-3121.00:1000.still_hard: Client volume is uncertain and seasonal; forecast quality only shows months later.
11-3121.00:1000.human_edge: Deciding how much risk to carry between fixed staff and flex, and getting site managers to commit to their numbers.

ambition.what: Quarterly rolling forecast per site and shift, instead of one yearly plan, timed before the seasonal flex peak.

11-3121.00:1000.altitude: The director moves from compiling numbers to setting the fixed-versus-flex policy per site with operations.

reach.learn: Open requisitions from the approved plan before the peak, not after.
Share one set of volume drivers between HR and Finance.

evidence.claim: Workday Work Intelligence (beta) cut a planned 50 hires to 42 in a demo by planning from tasks.
Personnel forecasts should show scenarios, not one number, on the analyst's metric layer.

assumptions: Operations has a volume forecast per site, even if rough.
Aggregated forecasts use no personal data beyond what Power BI already holds.
unknowns: Who in operations owns volume forecasts and how often they change.
Whether agency hours can be tied to sites and shifts.
research_questions: Would last year's model have predicted the actual flex peak within 15%?
Will site managers fill a fixed-format volume form each quarter?
Can agency portal data be joined to AFAS cost centres without manual mapping?

11-3121.00:1004.short: Read new labour law, court rulings and CAO news and judge what they mean for Noordhaven.

steps.what: Scan newsletters, government sites, union and court sources for changes
Read items, filter relevance and summarise the point

loop.input: Source item text plus a short profile of Noordhaven (CAOs, sites, flex use, policies)
loop.output: Relevance label, two-line summary with quoted passage and link, and affected policy
loop.check: Every claim must quote the source; links are checked to resolve; items without a quote are dropped
loop.stop: One pass per item, token cap per item; on failure the item goes to the digest as 'unread'
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance depends on free legal text; keyword filters flood or miss items.

steps.what: Assess impact on CAO talks, policies, costs and legal risk

11-3121.00:1004.design: A scheduled job fetches fixed sources (rechtspraak.nl, overheid.nl, Staatscourant, FNV, CNV, employer association pages) into a SharePoint list, and a bounded model step labels relevance and writes cited summaries for a weekly digest in Teams. 11-3121.00:1002.short: Build, schedule, run and score applicant tests such as forklift practicals and reading tests; check they work.

steps.what: Build or update test questions and practical checklists

loop.input: Job profile, safety instructions, required certificate content
loop.output: Draft question bank and practical checklist with answer keys
loop.check: Recruiter and site safety lead review every item before use; no personality or emotion inference items
loop.stop: One draft per test version; rejected items rewritten by the recruiter
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions must reflect each site's actual work instructions written in free text

steps.what: Schedule tests and invite candidates by mail
Run the test on site or online with the candidate
Score results and record them in Recruitee
Check test pass rates against 90-day retention and group gaps

11-3121.00:1002.design: Configure Recruitee self-scheduling and templates for test invites; a tablet form (Microsoft Forms or a small Power App) scores multiple-choice and practical checklists by code and writes the result into Recruitee for recruiter sign-off. A Power BI page links test results to AFAS 90-day retention; a bounded model step only drafts new question items for human review.
11-3121.00:1002.previous_blocker: Tests ran on paper per site, so scores never reached a system and nobody could check whether tests predicted who stayed.
11-3121.00:1002.enabler_now: Low-code forms and the Recruitee API are quick to wire with AI-assisted coding; question drafting is cheap.
11-3121.00:1002.still_hard: Small numbers per test version make validity checks weak; tests that decide on candidates fall under GDPR Art. 22 and later the AI Act high-risk regime.
11-3121.00:1002.human_edge: Watching a candidate drive a reach truck safely and judging nerves versus lack of skill; deciding pass or fail stays with a person.

ambition.what: A yearly test validity report per site showing which tests predict 90-day retention.

11-3121.00:1002.altitude: Scheduling and paperwork drop out; the recruiter owns test design per role family with evidence of what predicts staying.
